questions.question: A transformer has a turns ratio Ns/Np of 10. If the primary coil is powered with 220 V AC, what is the secondary output voltage in Volts?
When high current passes through a conductor, what parasitic magnetic effect pushes current density predominantly toward the outer perimeter of the wire?
questions.correct_answer: skin effect
questions.explanation: At high frequencies or currents, internal self-induced eddy currents oppose current flow in the center, crowding alternating current toward the conductor's outer skin.

questions.question: A domestic electrical installer replaces a blown 5 A fuse with a 30 A fuse wire to prevent it from tripping repeatedly. What primary hazard is created by this action?
questions.correct_answer: fire
questions.explanation: An oversized 30 A fuse allows dangerous overcurrents to pass without melting, causing household wiring to overheat, melt insulation, and ignite electrical fires.

questions.question: What electrical component acts as a non-mechanical electronic switch and amplifier, replacing early vacuum tubes?
questions.correct_answer: transistor
questions.explanation: The semiconductor transistor (invented in 1947) controls large collector currents via small base signals, serving as the universal solid-state amplifier and digital switch.

questions.question: An engineer evaluates whether stepping up transmission voltage tenfold (from 10 kV to 100 kV) reduces cable I²R power dissipation by a factor of 100 for the same delivered power. Is this calculation correct? Answer yes or no.
questions.correct_answer: yes
questions.explanation: Since P = VI, a 10× increase in V drops current I to 1/10th. Power loss in cables is P_loss = I²R; reducing current by 10 cuts power loss by (1/10)² = 1/100.

questions.question: A homeowner proposes connecting a standard electric water heater rated 110 V directly to a 220 V supply outlet. Will the power dissipated increase by a factor of 4? Answer yes or no.
questions.correct_answer: yes
questions.explanation: Power is P = V² / R. Doubling voltage from 110 V to 220 V across fixed resistance R quadruples power dissipation (2² = 4), which will rapidly burn out the heating element.

questions.question: A student claims that an ideal step-up transformer delivers more electrical energy per second from its secondary coil than it absorbs through its primary coil. Is this claim physically possible? Answer yes or no.
questions.correct_answer: no
questions.explanation: By the first law of thermodynamics (conservation of energy), no passive machine or transformer can output more energy or power than it receives (efficiency η ≤ 100%).

questions.question: An electrician evaluates connecting all electrical ceiling fans in series rather than parallel to save wiring cost. Is this proposed installation acceptable for a standard home? Answer yes or no.
questions.correct_answer: no
questions.explanation: In series, switching off one fan would stop all fans, and adding fans would divide the supply voltage, causing every fan to run sluggishly at a fraction of rated speed.

questions.question: A factory considers replacing copper transmission cables with aluminum cables of the exact same diameter. Will line resistance increase or decrease? Answer increase or decrease.
questions.correct_answer: increase
questions.explanation: Aluminum has higher electrical resistivity (ρ_Al ≈ 2.8 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m) than copper (ρ_Cu ≈ 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m). For identical dimensions, aluminum wire resistance is ~60% higher.

questions.question: A vehicle mechanic tests a car battery and finds its open-circuit EMF is 12.6 V, but its terminal voltage collapses to 4.0 V while cranking the engine. Does this evaluation indicate excessive internal resistance? Answer yes or no.
questions.correct_answer: yes
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage V = E - Ir. A severe voltage collapse from 12.6 V down to 4.0 V indicates high internal resistance (Ir = 8.6 V), showing the battery is degraded or sulfated.

questions.question: Why does a bird safely perch on a 33 kV overhead transmission line, but electrocutes itself if its wing simultaneously brushes the steel pylon?
options: Brushing the grounded steel pylon completes a high-voltage path to Earth across a 33,000 V potential difference
The pylon carries positive magnetic charges that attract the bird
Steel reflects electrical currents into the bird's feathers
The bird loses its electrical capacitance upon touching steel
questions.correct_answer: Brushing the grounded steel pylon completes a high-voltage path to Earth across a 33,000 V potential difference
questions.explanation: On a single wire, ΔV across the bird's feet is negligible. Touching the grounded steel pylon subjects the bird to the full 33 kV line-to-earth potential difference, driving a massive fatal current.

questions.question: What happens to the magnetic field pattern of a long solenoid if an iron rod is inserted along its central axis while carrying a steady current?
options: The magnetic flux density increases hundreds of times because iron has very high magnetic permeability
The magnetic field collapses to zero because iron absorbs magnetic lines
The solenoid converts from an electromagnet into an electrostatic capacitor
Current through the solenoid stops flowing immediately
questions.correct_answer: The magnetic flux density increases hundreds of times because iron has very high magnetic permeability
questions.explanation: Iron's relative permeability μ_r is typically 1,000–5,000. It aligns its internal magnetic domains with the solenoid's field, massively increasing the interior magnetic flux density B = μ_r μ₀ n I.

questions.question: In a household lighting circuit, two identical 60 W bulbs are wired in parallel. If one bulb burns out, how does the brightness of the surviving bulb change?
options: Its brightness remains completely unchanged because it still receives the full 220 V mains supply
Its brightness doubles because it receives all the current
Its brightness is halved
It turns off immediately
questions.correct_answer: Its brightness remains completely unchanged because it still receives the full 220 V mains supply
questions.explanation: In parallel, each branch is independent and connected across the constant 220 V mains. The voltage across and current through the surviving bulb remain unchanged, preserving its brightness.

questions.question: Why is an Earth wire connected directly to the metallic body of an electric clothes iron rather than to its heating element?
options: If an internal insulation fault touches the live wire to the metal chassis, fault current is safely diverted to ground to trip the breaker
The earth wire supplies additional current to heat the metal chassis
The earth wire prevents the iron from rusting
Connecting the earth wire to the element would double electricity bills
questions.correct_answer: If an internal insulation fault touches the live wire to the metal chassis, fault current is safely diverted to ground to trip the breaker
questions.explanation: Grounding the metal chassis ensures that if live conductor insulation chafes and touches the frame, the low-impedance earth path safely drains current and blows the fuse rather than electrocuting the user.

questions.question: Why does an electric generator armature experience strong mechanical resistance (torque opposition) when connected to a heavy electrical load?
options: By Lenz's law, induced currents create opposing magnetic forces that resist the mechanical rotation driving them
The generator bearings overheat and seize under current
Electrons become heavier as they carry electric current
The load pushes electric voltage backwards through the mechanical drive shaft
questions.correct_answer: By Lenz's law, induced currents create opposing magnetic forces that resist the mechanical rotation driving them
questions.explanation: Supplying power draws current through the armature. This current in the stator magnetic field experiences a counter-torque (F = BIL) opposing rotation, requiring more mechanical input power to maintain speed.

questions.question: What causes the high-frequency buzzing sound heard near large electrical substations and high-power transformers?
options: Magnetostriction causing periodic mechanical strain in the core at twice the AC grid frequency (100 Hz or 120 Hz)
Electrons arcing through the transformer cooling oil
Radio waves bouncing off substation fences
Cooling fans rotating at 100,000 RPM
questions.correct_answer: Magnetostriction causing periodic mechanical strain in the core at twice the AC grid frequency (100 Hz or 120 Hz)
questions.explanation: Transformer core laminations microscopically deform under alternating magnetic fields twice per cycle regardless of magnetic polarity, vibrating at 2f = 100 Hz (for 50 Hz grids) and radiating an audible hum.

questions.question: Why are copper conductors in high-voltage power lines suspended from tall pylons using ceramic or glass insulator discs rather than metal brackets?
options: Ceramics have enormous dielectric breakdown strength and high resistivity, preventing current from shorting to the grounded steel tower
Ceramics are flexible and absorb wind turbulence better than metal
Metal brackets absorb electricity and reduce voltage
Ceramics eliminate lightning strikes completely
questions.correct_answer: Ceramics have enormous dielectric breakdown strength and high resistivity, preventing current from shorting to the grounded steel tower
questions.explanation: High voltages (hundreds of kilovolts) would instantly flash over to grounded steel towers if supported by conductors. Ceramic disc strings provide the required creeping distance and dielectric barrier.

questions.question: Why does a DC series motor run dangerously fast (overspeed runaway) if started with no mechanical load connected?
options: Armature current and field flux are identical; at low load, field flux becomes very weak, forcing speed to soar to generate required back-EMF
The motor generates infinite electrical power when unloaded
Friction in the commutator becomes negative at zero load
A series motor has no magnetic field poles
questions.correct_answer: Armature current and field flux are identical; at low load, field flux becomes very weak, forcing speed to soar to generate required back-EMF
questions.explanation: In a series motor, field flux Φ ∝ I_a. Under zero load, I_a drops, weakening the field. Because speed N ∝ E_b / Φ, an extremely small flux causes rotational speed to rise dangerously, risking mechanical destruction.

questions.question: In a laboratory, a technician tests two parallel current-carrying wires. If the current in both wires is doubled and their separation distance is doubled, what happens to the force per unit length?
options: The force per unit length doubles
The force per unit length quadruples
The force per unit length remains unchanged
The force per unit length is halved
questions.correct_answer: The force per unit length doubles

questions.question: Why does an incandescent light bulb usually burn out at the exact moment it is switched on, rather than after running steadily for hours?
options: Cold tungsten filament has very low resistance, drawing a massive inrush current surge that thermally stresses any thinned section
The switch creates an electrostatic shock wave
Voltage surges to 10,000 V every time a wall switch closes
Cold glass absorbs all visible light and cracks the filament
questions.correct_answer: Cold tungsten filament has very low resistance, drawing a massive inrush current surge that thermally stresses any thinned section
questions.explanation: Tungsten resistance at room temperature is roughly 1/10th to 1/15th of its operating resistance at 2500°C. Turning on the switch triggers a huge current surge (I = V/R_cold) that vaporizes the thinnest filament segment.

questions.question: How does a lightning arrester protect electrical substations against high-voltage atmospheric surges?
options: Its non-linear metal-oxide varistor conducts negligible current at operating voltage, but drops to near-zero resistance during a surge to divert energy to ground
It catches lightning in a giant glass capacitor for storage
It turns high-voltage electricity into radio waves directed at clouds
It cuts off all power to consumer homes during rain
questions.correct_answer: Its non-linear metal-oxide varistor conducts negligible current at operating voltage, but drops to near-zero resistance during a surge to divert energy to ground
questions.explanation: Zinc-oxide (ZnO) surge arresters exhibit highly non-linear resistance. At normal line voltages they act as open circuits; when lightning creates a kilovolt spike, they conduct heavily, clamping voltage safely.

questions.question: Why does a step-down transformer require thicker copper wire for its secondary coil than for its primary coil?
options: The secondary delivers a much higher current, requiring a larger cross-sectional area to minimize I²R resistive heating
The secondary coil operates at higher voltage and needs mechanical support
Thicker wire increases the turns ratio automatically
Secondary coils are exposed to higher magnetic field radiation
questions.correct_answer: The secondary delivers a much higher current, requiring a larger cross-sectional area to minimize I²R resistive heating
questions.explanation: Because power P = VI is conserved, stepping down voltage forces secondary current Is to be much higher than primary Ip. Thicker wire (larger area A) lowers resistance R = ρL/A to safely handle heavy current.

questions.question: Why is an analog voltmeter designed with an extremely high internal resistance, whereas an ammeter is designed with near-zero internal resistance?
options: To minimize their perturbation of the circuit conditions they are intended to measure
To prevent the pointer from spinning too quickly
To make voltmeters compatible with alternating current
Because voltmeters must store high electrical charges like capacitors
questions.correct_answer: To minimize their perturbation of the circuit conditions they are intended to measure
questions.explanation: An ideal voltmeter draws zero branch current (R_v → ∞), leaving circuit operation unaltered. An ideal ammeter introduces zero voltage drop (R_a → 0), leaving loop current unchanged.

questions.question: Why is pure silicon doped with pentavalent phosphorus atoms to create an n-type semiconductor?
options: Phosphorus donates extra free conduction electrons that significantly increase electrical conductivity
Phosphorus captures electrons to create positive holes
Phosphorus transforms silicon into a superconductor at room temperature
Phosphorus increases the electrical resistance of the silicon crystal
questions.correct_answer: Phosphorus donates extra free conduction electrons that significantly increase electrical conductivity
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has 5 valence electrons. Four form covalent bonds with adjacent silicon atoms, while the fifth is easily liberated into the conduction band as a mobile negative charge carrier.

questions.question: Why does a p-n junction diode allow electric current to flow easily under forward bias, but blocks current under reverse bias?
options: Forward bias lowers the depletion barrier allowing majority carriers to cross; reverse bias widens the depletion layer and barrier potential
Forward bias destroys all electrons inside the semiconductor
Reverse bias turns the p-type region into an electrical insulator
Diodes contain miniature mechanical valves that shut under reverse polarity
questions.correct_answer: Forward bias lowers the depletion barrier allowing majority carriers to cross; reverse bias widens the depletion layer and barrier potential
questions.explanation: Under forward bias (p-side positive, n-side negative), the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential, thinning the depletion zone and allowing charge carriers to cross freely. Reverse bias widens the barrier.

questions.question: What happens when an alternating current of 50 Hz is passed through a normal moving-coil galvanometer?
options: The pointer vibrates imperceptibly about zero because the average torque over each complete cycle is zero
The pointer deflects steadily to the maximum scale value
The galvanometer coil burns out immediately within 1 microsecond
The pointer rotates continuously like an electric fan
questions.correct_answer: The pointer vibrates imperceptibly about zero because the average torque over each complete cycle is zero
questions.explanation: Torque reverses direction every 10 ms (50 Hz AC). Due to rotational inertia, the mechanical coil assembly cannot track this rapid alternation, displaying a net deflection of zero.

questions.question: Why does a Faraday cage protect sensitive electronics and occupants inside an automobile from a direct lightning strike?
options: Charges reside exclusively on the outer conductive surface of a hollow metal shell, leaving zero electric field inside
The metal roof absorbs all electrical charge into nuclear mass
Rubber tires insulate the vehicle completely from cloud voltages
Lightning cannot strike objects moving faster than 10 km/h
questions.correct_answer: Charges reside exclusively on the outer conductive surface of a hollow metal shell, leaving zero electric field inside
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law, electrostatic charges on a conductor redistribute entirely along the outer surface. The electric field inside any hollow metallic enclosure remains strictly zero (electrostatic shielding).

questions.question: How does a rheostat regulate the speed of an electric motor or the brightness of a lamp?
options: By adjusting the length of resistive wire in series, varying total circuit resistance and controlling current
By converting direct current into radio waves
By altering the chemical voltage of the power source
By changing the physical frequency of electron oscillations
questions.correct_answer: By adjusting the length of resistive wire in series, varying total circuit resistance and controlling current
questions.explanation: A sliding contact alters effective wire length L. Since R = ρL/A, varying resistance adjusts current (I = V/R) and voltage delivered to the connected load.

questions.question: Why does an electric current flowing through a coiled wire produce a much stronger magnetic field than the same current in a straight wire?
options: Magnetic fields from each adjacent loop add vectorially along the central axis of the coil
Coiling a wire increases the electric charge of electrons
Coiling a wire slows down the speed of electricity
Straight wires absorb their own magnetic fields
questions.correct_answer: Magnetic fields from each adjacent loop add vectorially along the central axis of the coil
questions.explanation: By superposition, each circular turn generates a magnetic field at the center. Coiling N turns multiplies the axial magnetic field strength N-fold (B = μ₀NI / 2R).

questions.question: An electrical contractor proposes wiring lighting fixtures and high-power air conditioners on the same 5 A circuit breaker to cut installation costs. How do you evaluate this proposal?
options: Hazardous and unacceptable: air conditioning compressors draw heavy surge currents that will cause continuous tripping or overheat 5 A wiring
Acceptable and cost-efficient for modern homes
Acceptable only if all lighting fixtures use incandescent bulbs
Hazardous only during winter months
questions.correct_answer: Hazardous and unacceptable: air conditioning compressors draw heavy surge currents that will cause continuous tripping or overheat 5 A wiring
questions.explanation: Air conditioners require dedicated 15 A or 20 A circuits with heavy-gauge cable. Operating on a 5 A lighting circuit will trip the breaker or melt wiring, creating a serious fire hazard.

questions.question: A utility company evaluates whether to transmit 100 MW of power at 400 kV instead of 100 kV across a 200 km line with a resistance of 10 Ω. What is the reduction in I²R transmission power loss?
options: Power loss drops from 10 MW down to 0.625 MW (a 16-fold reduction in loss)
Power loss drops from 100 MW down to 10 MW
Power loss remains exactly identical
Power loss drops to zero Watts completely
questions.correct_answer: Power loss drops from 10 MW down to 0.625 MW (a 16-fold reduction in loss)
questions.explanation: At 100 kV: I = 100 MW / 100 kV = 1000 A. Loss = I²R = (1000)² × 10 = 10 MW. At 400 kV: I = 100 MW / 400 kV = 250 A. Loss = (250)² × 10 = 0.625 MW. Loss is reduced by (400/100)² = 16 times.

questions.question: A student attempts to operate a standard step-down transformer (designed for 220 V 50 Hz AC) on a 12 V DC car battery. What is the predicted operational result?
options: The secondary output voltage will be zero after an initial transient, and the primary winding will overheat from excessive DC current
The transformer will step down 12 V DC to 1.2 V DC smoothly
The transformer will convert the DC battery into 220 V AC electricity
The battery will immediately recharge itself to 100%
questions.correct_answer: The secondary output voltage will be zero after an initial transient, and the primary winding will overheat from excessive DC current
questions.explanation: Steady DC lacks inductive reactance (X_L = 2πfL = 0). Only low ohmic resistance limits primary current, drawing massive current that overheats the coil while generating zero steady secondary EMF (dΦ/dt = 0).

questions.question: An industrial facility considers replacing traditional lead-tin wire fuses with a modern Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker (ELCB / RCCB). What critical safety improvement justifies this evaluation?
options: ELCB detects low-milliampere ground leakage currents (e.g. 30 mA) to prevent human fatal electrocution, which wire fuses cannot detect
ELCB eliminates electricity consumption from the factory
ELCB allows machines to run without any electrical power
Wire fuses conduct more current than circuit breakers
questions.correct_answer: ELCB detects low-milliampere ground leakage currents (e.g. 30 mA) to prevent human fatal electrocution, which wire fuses cannot detect
questions.explanation: Fuses only blow on huge overcurrents (e.g. >15 A) and will not protect a person being electrocuted at 50–100 mA. An RCCB trips within 30 ms upon detecting tiny current imbalances (≥30 mA).

questions.question: A consumer evaluates two light bulbs: a 10 W LED bulb producing 800 lumens versus a 60 W incandescent bulb producing 800 lumens. Over 5000 hours at 8 Taka per kWh, how much money does the LED save?
options: 2000 Taka
400 Taka
1600 Taka
2400 Taka
questions.correct_answer: 2000 Taka
questions.explanation: Power difference = 60 W - 10 W = 50 W = 0.05 kW. Energy saved = 0.05 kW × 5000 h = 250 kWh. Cost saved = 250 kWh × 8 Taka/kWh = 2000 Taka.

questions.question: An engineer tests a transformer core made of solid non-laminated cast steel. Compared to a laminated silicon-steel core of identical dimensions, what negative performance outcome occurs?
options: Massive eddy current heating losses will severely reduce efficiency and cause the transformer to overheat
The secondary voltage will double
The transformer will operate with 100% efficiency
The solid core eliminates all magnetic hysteresis
questions.correct_answer: Massive eddy current heating losses will severely reduce efficiency and cause the transformer to overheat
questions.explanation: Solid steel presents large unbroken cross-sections for induced eddy currents, generating huge I²R heating losses that degrade efficiency and threaten thermal breakdown of insulation.

questions.question: A technician assesses a circuit where a 12 V battery powers an uninsulated immersion heater submerged in distilled water versus saltwater. What difference in behavior will occur?
options: Saltwater conducts current through dissolved ions, creating electrolysis and stray current leakage, whereas distilled water conducts almost nothing
Distilled water explodes upon contact with electric current
Saltwater has infinite electrical resistance and stops all current
Both waters behave identically as perfect insulators
questions.correct_answer: Saltwater conducts current through dissolved ions, creating electrolysis and stray current leakage, whereas distilled water conducts almost nothing
questions.explanation: Pure distilled water lacks free charge carriers. Dissolved salt (NaCl) dissociates into mobile Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, turning the bath into an electrolyte with low electrical resistance.

questions.question: An inventor claims to have developed a DC generator that produces 500 W of electrical output while requiring only 300 W of mechanical shaft input power. How do you evaluate this claim?
options: The claim violates the first law of thermodynamics (conservation of energy) and is impossible
The claim is possible if superconducting magnets are used
The claim is possible if the generator spins faster than 3000 RPM
The claim is valid because electromagnetic induction creates free energy
questions.correct_answer: The claim violates the first law of thermodynamics (conservation of energy) and is impossible
questions.explanation: An output of 500 W from 300 W input implies an efficiency of 167%, which violates the law of conservation of energy. No device can generate more power than it consumes.

questions.question: In evaluating home electrical safety, why is it critical that single-pole switches and circuit breakers are installed on the LIVE wire rather than the NEUTRAL wire?
options: Opening the switch disconnects high voltage from the appliance; switching the neutral leaves the appliance live at 220 V even when turned off
Neutral wires cannot conduct current through a switch
Installing switches on the live wire halves the electricity bill
The neutral wire carries twice as much voltage as the live wire
questions.correct_answer: Opening the switch disconnects high voltage from the appliance; switching the neutral leaves the appliance live at 220 V even when turned off
questions.explanation: If a switch is on the neutral wire, opening it stops current but leaves the entire internal appliance circuitry live at 220 V relative to earth. An unsuspecting user touching it risks severe shock.

questions.question: A student measures the resistance of an incandescent bulb when cold with an ohmmeter (reads 40 Ω) and calculates its power at 220 V as P = V²/R = 220²/40 = 1210 W. However, the bulb is labeled 100 W. How do you evaluate this discrepancy?
options: The calculation is flawed because tungsten's operating resistance at 2500°C is over 10 times higher (~484 Ω) than its cold resistance
The manufacturer mislabeled the bulb
Ohm's law does not apply to electric light bulbs
The ohmmeter damaged the bulb's filament
questions.correct_answer: The calculation is flawed because tungsten's operating resistance at 2500°C is over 10 times higher (~484 Ω) than its cold resistance
questions.explanation: Metals exhibit positive temperature coefficients. Cold tungsten resistance is ~40 Ω, but white-hot operating resistance is R = V²/P = 220²/100 = 484 Ω. Evaluating power using cold resistance is invalid.

questions.question: An audio amplifier manufacturer evaluates using gold plating on audio jack connectors rather than bare copper. What technical justification supports this decision?
options: Gold does not oxidize or tarnish in air, preserving low-resistance contact over years of use
Gold has much lower electrical resistivity than copper
Gold converts audio signals into laser beams
Gold amplifies the bass frequencies mechanically
questions.correct_answer: Gold does not oxidize or tarnish in air, preserving low-resistance contact over years of use
questions.explanation: While copper is slightly more conductive than gold, copper readily oxidizes into resistive copper oxide. Chemically inert gold never tarnishes, ensuring corrosion-free audio contact.

questions.question: A solar microgrid installation evaluates connecting two 12 V, 100 Ah deep-cycle batteries in series versus parallel to power a 24 V inverter. What is the correct battery configuration?
options: Series connection: voltages add to produce 24 V at 100 Ah capacity
Parallel connection: voltages add to produce 24 V at 200 Ah capacity
Parallel connection: produces 12 V at 100 Ah capacity
Series connection: produces 12 V at 200 Ah capacity
questions.correct_answer: Series connection: voltages add to produce 24 V at 100 Ah capacity
questions.explanation: Connecting batteries in series adds their voltages (12 V + 12 V = 24 V) while capacity remains 100 Ah, perfectly matching the required 24 V inverter input.

questions.question: A safety auditor inspects an industrial motor installation and finds the metallic ground wire has an electrical resistance of 25 Ω. How do you evaluate this grounding installation?
options: Defective and hazardous: ground resistance must be very low (< 1 to 5 Ω) so that fault currents can trip protective breakers instantly
Acceptable because high ground resistance saves electric power
Acceptable because ground resistance does not affect human safety
Defective because ground wires should have infinite resistance
questions.correct_answer: Defective and hazardous: ground resistance must be very low (< 1 to 5 Ω) so that fault currents can trip protective breakers instantly
questions.explanation: If a live fault occurs on a frame with 25 Ω grounding, fault current to ground is only 220 V / 25 Ω ≈ 8.8 A—insufficient to instantly trip a 16 A breaker, leaving the frame at a lethal potential.

questions.question: An electronics design team evaluates using a silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductor switch instead of a standard silicon MOSFET for high-voltage electric vehicle inverters. What performance advantage justifies this evaluation?
options: SiC has a much wider bandgap, allowing higher breakdown voltage, faster switching speeds, and operation at significantly higher temperatures
SiC eliminates the need for electric batteries in vehicles
SiC is an organic polymer that dissolves in water
SiC switches have zero electrical resistance at room temperature
questions.correct_answer: SiC has a much wider bandgap, allowing higher breakdown voltage, faster switching speeds, and operation at significantly higher temperatures
questions.explanation: Wide-bandgap semiconductors (SiC and GaN) support 10× higher electric fields before breakdown, switching higher voltages with drastically lower conduction and switching losses.

questions.question: A hospital evaluates backup power solutions and decides to install an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) backed by a diesel generator. Why is the battery UPS essential rather than relying solely on the generator?
options: The battery UPS provides instantaneous (< 10 ms) seamless power takeover, preventing life-support equipment from rebooting while the diesel generator starts up
The generator cannot produce 220 V alternating current
The battery UPS generates its own diesel fuel
Diesel generators only supply direct current
questions.correct_answer: The battery UPS provides instantaneous (< 10 ms) seamless power takeover, preventing life-support equipment from rebooting while the diesel generator starts up
questions.explanation: Generators require 10 to 30 seconds to crank and reach steady operating speed. Battery-inverter UPS systems transfer in milliseconds, bridging the critical blackout window.

questions.question: A homeowner installs lightning protection on their house roof using a 1-meter pointed copper rod connected via a heavy copper down-conductor to a buried ground plate. How do you evaluate this installation?
options: Proper and effective: the sharp point encourages corona discharge to neutralize clouds and provides a low-resistance path to Earth if struck
Ineffective: lightning rods attract all lightning from the entire city directly into the house
Ineffective: lightning rods must be made of plastic to repel electricity
Hazardous: the copper rod must be connected to the domestic live mains wire
questions.correct_answer: Proper and effective: the sharp point encourages corona discharge to neutralize clouds and provides a low-resistance path to Earth if struck
questions.explanation: Franklin's design works by leaking charge from sharp points to prevent ionization, and providing a heavy copper conductor (≥50 mm²) to route any direct strike safely into the earth.

questions.question: A technician investigates why a 10 kW industrial DC motor slows down and loses torque under heavy load. What is the most plausible electrical diagnostic evaluation?
options: Excessive voltage drop along thin power supply cables combined with worn commutator brushes reducing armature current
The motor has developed negative resistance
The Earth's magnetic field has reversed polarity
Electrons are colliding with air molecules inside the armature
questions.correct_answer: Excessive voltage drop along thin power supply cables combined with worn commutator brushes reducing armature current
questions.explanation: Under high load, increased current causes large I·R cable voltage drops, starving motor terminals. Worn brushes create poor contact resistance, further dropping armature voltage and torque.

questions.question: An engineer evaluates whether a step-up transformer can be built with equal numbers of primary and secondary turns (Np = Ns) by making the secondary wire twice as thick. What is the outcome?
options: The output voltage will equal the input voltage (Vs = Vp); it functions as an isolation transformer, not a step-up transformer
The output voltage will double because the wire is thicker
The output voltage will be halved
The transformer will catch fire immediately
questions.correct_answer: The output voltage will equal the input voltage (Vs = Vp); it functions as an isolation transformer, not a step-up transformer
questions.explanation: Voltage ratio is determined strictly by the turns ratio: Vs / Vp = Ns / Np. Wire thickness affects current-carrying capacity, not voltage transformation.

questions.question: A student connects three identical 12 V light bulbs in series to a 12 V battery. How does their total light output compare to connecting the same three bulbs in parallel to the same battery?
options: The parallel configuration outputs 9 times more total light power than the series configuration
The series configuration outputs 3 times more light power
Both configurations produce identical total light output
The parallel configuration outputs 27 times more light power
questions.correct_answer: The parallel configuration outputs 9 times more total light power than the series configuration
questions.explanation: Let bulb resistance be R. In series, R_s = 3R; P_series = V² / (3R). In parallel, R_p = R/3; P_parallel = V² / (R/3) = 3V² / R. Ratio P_parallel / P_series = (3V²/R) / (V²/3R) = 9.

questions.question: An electrical utility evaluates whether to use DC or AC for a new 1000-kilometer subsea undersea transmission cable (HVDC vs HVAC). Why is High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) evaluated as superior for long subsea cables?
options: Subsea AC cables suffer from enormous capacitive charging currents that choke power transfer, whereas DC suffers zero continuous capacitive reactive loss
DC travels twice as fast through seawater as AC
Direct current does not require copper or aluminum conductors
Transformers only operate on underwater direct current
questions.correct_answer: Subsea AC cables suffer from enormous capacitive charging currents that choke power transfer, whereas DC suffers zero continuous capacitive reactive loss
questions.explanation: The large capacitance between cable conductor and seawater draws massive reactive charging current under AC (I_c = 2πfCV), limiting AC transmission to <50 km. HVDC eliminates steady-state capacitive reactance.

questions.question: A student proposes that connecting an extra resistor in parallel across an existing circuit branch will increase the overall equivalent resistance of the network. How do you evaluate this proposition?
options: The proposition is false: adding a parallel resistor always decreases equivalent resistance because it provides an additional conduction path
The proposition is true: all resistors add resistance to circuits regardless of how they are connected
The proposition is true only if the added resistor has a resistance greater than 1000 Ω
The proposition is true only in direct current circuits
questions.correct_answer: The proposition is false: adding a parallel resistor always decreases equivalent resistance because it provides an additional conduction path
questions.explanation: In parallel, total conductance G_total = G_existing + 1/R_new > G_existing. Since equivalent resistance is R_eq = 1/G_total, adding any parallel branch strictly decreases equivalent resistance.
